title: The Website That Vanished at Midnight
description: A bakery's website went down during a holiday sale. Investigate the cloud incident.

briefing.clientMessage: This is Martha, owner of The Digital Bakery. Last night was our biggest sale of the year, but at 11:59 PM our website just stopped working. Customers got 503 errors, and we lost thousands in sales. I don't understand what happened—we didn't deploy anything unusual, and our server team is stumped. Can you help me figure out what went wrong?

evidence.label: Load Balancer Status
evidence.text:
HTTP Status from ALB: 503 Service Unavailable
Error Message: Service Temporarily Unavailable
Timestamp: 2024-12-15 23:59:42

The ALB is returning 503 to all requests.
This means either:
- No healthy targets available
- The targets are not responding
- Configuration issue at the load balancer
evidence.hint: Rosa: Think about what a 503 error means. The ALB has no healthy backends to send traffic to. Check the target group status.

evidence.label: Metrics & Monitoring
evidence.text:
$ aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name CPUUtilization

EC2 Instance CPU Utilization:
2024-12-15T23:30:00Z  85.2%  ← Spike
2024-12-15T23:45:00Z  20.1%  ← Normal
2024-12-15T23:59:00Z  18.5%  ← Still normal

Target Group Healthy Host Count:
2024-12-15T23:50:00Z  2  (healthy)
2024-12-15T23:59:00Z  0  (UNHEALTHY)
2024-12-15T00:05:00Z  0  (still unhealthy)

Health Check Failures (both instances):
Reason: Request timeout (no response on port 80)
Last successful check: 23:58:30
evidence.hint: Rosa: Both instances failed health checks at the exact same moment (23:59). What could cause both to suddenly stop responding on port 80?

evidence.label: Target Group Configuration
evidence.text:
$ aws elbv2 describe-target-groups --names app-servers

TargetGroupName: app-servers
HealthCheckProtocol: HTTP
HealthCheckPort: 80
HealthCheckPath: /health
HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 30

Registered Targets:

1. i-0abc123def456ghi
   State: unhealthy
   Reason: "Target.ResponseCodeMismatch"
   Description: "Health checks failed with port 80 timeout"
   LastStatusChange: 2024-12-15 23:59:15

2. i-0xyz789uvw012rst  
   State: unhealthy
   Reason: "Target.ResponseCodeMismatch"
   Description: "Health checks failed with port 80 timeout"
   LastStatusChange: 2024-12-15 23:59:18

Both instances: NOT RESPONDING on port 80
evidence.hint: Rosa: Port 80 is where the ALB sends health checks. Why would both instances stop listening there at 23:59?

evidence.label: EC2 Instances
evidence.text:
$ aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids i-0abc123def456ghi i-0xyz789uvw012rst

Instance 1: i-0abc123def456ghi
State: running
CPU Utilization: 18.5%
Memory: Available
Disk Space: OK
Network: OK
Status Checks: Passed (system and instance)

Instance 2: i-0xyz789uvw012rst
State: running
CPU Utilization: 19.2%
Memory: Available
Disk Space: OK  
Network: OK
Status Checks: Passed (system and instance)

✓ Both instances are running and healthy
✓ No OS or hardware issues detected
✓ Application processes are running
✗ But unreachable on port 80 from ALB
evidence.hint: Rosa: The instances are running fine. So the problem must be with network connectivity or a security rule, right?

evidence.label: Audit Logs
evidence.hint: Rosa: This is the smoking gun. Someone deleted a critical security group rule. Who had access, and why would they do that?

evidence.label: Security Group Rules
evidence.text:
$ aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-web-instances

GroupId: sg-web-instances
GroupName: web-instances

Inbound Rules:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Protocol │ Port │ Source        │ Effect    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ TCP      │ 22   │ 0.0.0.0/0     │ ALLOW ⚠️  │
│ TCP      │ 443  │ sg-alb        │ ALLOW     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

❌ MISSING: TCP 80 from sg-alb (was deleted at 23:58:42)

Outbound Rules:
All traffic allowed

✓ Port 443 (HTTPS) allows ALB traffic
✗ Port 80 (HTTP) rule is GONE - ALB health checks blocked!
⚠️  SSH (port 22) is open to entire internet (0.0.0.0/0)
evidence.hint: The rule allowing ALB to reach the instances on port 80 is missing. This breaks the health check mechanism.

evidence.label: Recent Deployments
evidence.text:
$ aws codedeploy list-deployments

Deployment Summary:

2024-12-15 22:00:15 UTC - Deployment d-ABCD1234EF
Status: SUCCESS ✓
Version: 2.1.0
Instances Updated: 2
Duration: 45 seconds
Errors: None

Deployment Log:
[22:00:15] Starting deployment to i-0abc123def456ghi
[22:00:30] Application files transferred
[22:00:45] Service restarted - SUCCESS
[22:01:00] Health check passed
[22:01:15] Starting deployment to i-0xyz789uvw012rst
[22:01:30] Application files transferred
[22:01:45] Service restarted - SUCCESS
[22:02:00] Health check passed

✓ Both instances updated successfully
✓ No errors in deployment
✓ Application running fine 23:30-23:59 (2 hours)

Conclusion: Deployment is NOT the cause.
Issue occurred 1 hour 59 minutes AFTER deployment completed.
evidence.hint: The deployment worked fine and ran for almost 2 hours. Look for what changed at 23:59, not at 22:00.

rootCauses.text: CPU spike at 23:30 caused the instances to become unresponsive
The 22:00 code deployment had a hidden bug that crashed the app
Deleted security group rule removed ALB's access to instances on port 80
Database connection pool exhausted, instances couldn't respond
Distributed denial of service attack overwhelmed the instances

keyEvidence.text: CloudWatch metrics showing health check failures
CloudTrail log showing security group rule was revoked
Deployment logs showing successful deployment 2 hours prior
CPU spike at 23:30 before the outage
Application logs showing no errors or crashes

fixes.text: Re-add the TCP 80 inbound rule from sg-alb to sg-web-instances
Add more EC2 instances to handle the CPU load
Increase the database connection pool size
Enable AWS WAF to block the DDoS attack

explanation: The intern accidentally deleted the security group rule that allowed the ALB to communicate with the EC2 instances on port 80. Without this rule, the ALB's health checks couldn't reach the instances, causing them to be marked as unhealthy. Once an ALB has no healthy targets, it returns 503 Service Unavailable to all incoming requests. The CPU spike was a separate scheduled backup that had no connection to the outage. The fix is straightforward: restore the deleted inbound rule to allow TCP port 80 traffic from the ALB security group.
hiddenBonus: Port 22 (SSH) is open to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing anyone on the internet to attempt SSH login to your instances. This is a critical security risk. Use a security group that restricts SSH to specific IP addresses or a bastion host instead.
intro: Rosa: Your first client is Martha, who owns The Digital Bakery. Her website went down during their biggest sale of the year. Let's investigate.
outro: Rosa: Great work! You caught the security group misconfiguration. This is exactly the kind of subtle-but-critical issue we see in production. You're off to a strong start.
